new_statements.quote: There are a few general rules that govern the pronunciation of these forms. i) Primary stress always fall on the first syllable of a word. [p. 27] ... The first stress rule places heavy stress on the first syllable of every word and on the first syllable of the second member of a compound word, hence it applies iteratively to as many segments as meet the structural conditions for its application. The second rule reduces the stress on the second element of a compound word. (Primary stress is indicated by means of the symbol /´/, secondary stress by means of /˝/.) P.R.1. Stress Placement (SP) ... P.R.2. Stress Reduction (SR) [p. 124]
new_statements.citation: Andres, Susie. 1977. Description of Muria Gondi Phonology and Morphology with a Transformational Account of the Morphophonological Processes Employed. Ph.D. thesis, Department of Linguistics, Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (University of Poona), Pune. xxxiv+666 pp. Shodhganga hdl:10603/563349 (Vol. II hdl:10603/149218).
new_statements.locator: Chapter I Phonology, sec. 1.1.1, p. 27 (rule i); formal rule P.R.1 Stress Placement and P.R.2 Stress Reduction, p. 124; compound stress p. 37 fn. 16
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the first syllable of every word, without exception; in compounds each member keeps first-syllable stress but the second member is reduced to secondary stress. Stress is predictable (rule-assigned), not contrastive.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Only in compounds: the first syllable of the second (head) element carries secondary stress, stronger than other non-initial syllables (p. 37 fn. 16, p. 124 P.R.2). No rhythmic secondary stress described.
new_statements.exceptions: None for simple words ('always'). Compounds: first element's first syllable takes major stress, the head noun (second element) takes secondary stress (p. 37 fn. 16; p. 38; P.R.2 p. 124). Bound feminine classifier ha:ri: after kinship terms is weakly stressed (p. 37 fn. 16). Words with underlying long consonants show a very short stressed first syllable followed by a long second syllable (p. 33 fn. 11).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: 'the first syllable of a word'; the rule is stated for the pronunciation of stem forms and then formalized as P.R.1 applying to every phonological word and to each member of a compound (with the second member reduced to secondary stress by P.R.2). Stress is treated as non-contrastive and rule-assigned; vowel length is contrastive only in initial syllables (p. 27-28). Confidence is 'low' for east2340 only because the described variety is Western Muria, not Eastern Muria (see identity_note); as a statement about Sonapal Muria it is unambiguous.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is NOT about Eastern Muria. Andres 1977 describes the Muria Gondi of Sonapal village, Narayanpur Tahsil (intro p. 1), which Beine 1994/2013 p. 47 lists as test point mso in the WESTERN Muria group (Appendix A p. 96: 'Muria from Narayanpur Tehsil'); Beine's Eastern Muria (p. 49) = Lanjoda, Kondagaon Tehsil (mlj) and Raigarh, Umerkote Tehsil, Koraput/Nabarangpur, Odisha (gok), with only 69-73% intelligibility between the two groups. Glottolog itself files Andres (as 1978) under west2408 Western Muria [mut], which is a separate target in WORLD_TARGETS (scan verdict SOURCE-NAMED-UNREACHABLE; the thesis is now on file under east2340/ and can be reused there). Andres also notes (intro p. 5) that over half of Sonapal's residents descend from Abujhmarh Marias, so 'Muria Gondi' may be a misnomer even for her variety. The Far Western Muria statement (Mathew & Mathew 2013) belongs to farw1235 [fmu]. No first-hand description of Eastern Muria proper (east2340) was found.

sources.note: Ch. I Phonology p. 27: 'Primary stress always fall on the first syllable of a word'; p. 37 fn. 16: in compounds the first element's first syllable takes stronger stress than the second element's, whose first syllable is still stronger than other non-initial syllables; p. 124 P.R.1 Stress Placement puts heavy stress on the first syllable of every word and of the second member of a compound, P.R.2 reduces the compound's second element to secondary stress. Variety: Muria Gondi of Sonapal village, ~15 km E of Narayanpur, Narayanpur Tahsil, Bastar District (intro p. 1) = Beine's Western Muria test…

sources.note: SISTER variety farw1235 [fmu] (Kurkheda tehsil, Gadchiroli, Maharashtra), not Eastern Muria. Sec. 2.4 pp. 6-7: 'In general, words carry primary stress on the first syllable... in some sentence frames and for some phonological word types primary stress is carried by the final syllable'; sec. 9 pp. 67-68: 'Stress is not contrastive in Far Western Muria. Stress is phonetically realized by loudness, a rise in pitch and a slight lengthening of the vowel of the stressed syllable'; words with short V1 and tap/flap onset of syllable 2 get final stress with V1 reduction (uṛm 'louse', taras 'snake').

sources.citation: Beine, David K. 2013 [1994]. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Gondi-speaking Communities of Central India. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2013-006 (= M.A. thesis, San Diego State University, Spring 1994), 531 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or phonology (wordlists, RTT, attitudes). Defines the split: p. 47 'Western Muria. The western varieties of Sonapal (mso), Banchapai (mch), and Dhanora (mud) are more alike'; p. 49 'Eastern Muria. The eastern variety of Muria is found to the eastern side of Bastar District. The dialects of Raigarh (gok) and Lanjoda (mlj)...' (Appendix A p. 96: mlj = Muria from Lanjoda, Kondagaon Tehsil; gok = Gondi from Raigarh, Umrakot Tehsil, Koraput District, Orissa; mso = Muria from Narayanpur Tehsil); western-eastern intelligibility 69-73%.

sources.note: The only Muria thesis on Shodhganga is Andres 1977 (two records, hdl 10603/563349 Vol. I and 10603/149218 Vol. II). Other Gondi theses found are for Adilabad Gondi, Parsi Gondi of Mandla/Balaghat/Betul, Abujhmaria, Dandami Maria, Vidarbha Gondi — none Eastern Muria. No Muria phonology article in Crossref/OpenAlex.
Phoneme tables only, sourced from Mathew & Mathew 2013 (Far Western Muria); nothing on stress; no other Muria description cited.
